newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian banking sector's '96 profit up sharply.
newsitem.headline: Colombian banking sector's '96 profit up sharply.

text.p: The net profit of Colombia's banking sector rose 45.29 percent in 1996 over the previous year but its liabilities rose sharply as well, the country's Bank Superintendency reported.

It said the net profit of all Colombian banks, including the state-run Caja Agraria, totaled 494 billion pesos in 1996. But liabilities totaled 25.12 trillion pesos and were up 35.24 percent over 1995.

No reason was given for the increase in liablilities in the superintendency's annual report on the performance of the banking sector, but industry sources say the level of past-due loans rose substantially throughout the sector last year.
The superintendency said assets of the banking sector totaled 29.77 trillion pesos by year-end 1996, up 21.82 percent over 1995.
